text: Minister Iswaran will share more details of mid-career training programmes for the Info-Communications and Technology (ICT) sector at MCI's COS debate later.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Minister Josephine Teo and Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat will also elaborate on plans to increase reskilling capacity and to help workers make career transitions at the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and the Ministry of Education's (MOE's) COS debates respectively later today and tomorrow.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I will now share three key ways in which companies can play an important role in supporting this national effort – redesign, reskill and recruit.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Businesses should seek to actively redesign their jobs to create new opportunities for existing and new workers, including those in their 40s and 50s, even as they pursue enterprise transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As part of the Next Bound of SkillsFuture, businesses can now tap on the enhanced Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG), which includes consultancy services for job redesign.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: We want to make job redesign a key component for enterprise transformation.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As Mr Desmond Choo noted, when businesses grow and transform, they have an important role to play in actively reskilling their workers rather than poaching from others.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Next Bound of SkillsFuture will also see an enhanced focus on businesses driving enterprise and workforce transformation in tandem.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Three thousand dollars of the SFEC will be reserved for the latter.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: These outcomes may include wage increases, creation of skilled jobs for Singaporeans, job redesign and workers' training.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Businesses need to offer suitable placement opportunities for our mature workers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: The Government will support by giving a Hiring Incentive to employers who hire local jobseekers aged 40 and above through eligible reskilling programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Such programmes include Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs), Place-and-Train (PnT) programmes and career transition programmes by SkillsFuture Singapore's (SSG's) CET Centres.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: I urge all employers to come forward, transform their business and, at the same time, create new opportunities for all workers, including our older workers.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: This has always been a critical part of our growth strategy and an important chapter of the Singapore Story.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: Mr Chairman, if there is anything we have learnt from past challenges and the current COVID-19 situation, it is that we should never underestimate the strength and resilience of our people.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: As we battle COVID-19, we must also strive to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
text: And this year's MTI tagline is: "to emerge stronger".

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, as a small and open economy, Singapore must be nimble and responsive to developments in the global economy, in order to maintain our competitive advantage.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will foster innovation in Singapore by strengthening our innovation ecosystem and leveraging innovation to transform our industries and seize new growth opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will strengthen the innovation ecosystem to help companies harness technological change and bring new ideas to market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Ms Foo Mee Har asked about the research landscape in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As part of the Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2020 Plan (RIE2020), we provide strong support to our companies in their innovation activities, including translating research into commercially viable products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We have established technology consortia, which bring together companies and public sector researchers to collaborate on research projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Companies can join these consortia to keep up with research trends and tap on the expertise of our many researchers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our COIs that Ms Foo Mee Har asked about, provide specialised expertise to help companies translate problem statements into technology requirements.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Lee Yi Shyan asked about our digital ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In addition to our strong research and development (R&D) capabilities, we are also constantly building up other aspects of our pro-innovation ecosystem, including access to skilled global talent and a vibrant startup ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We have also set up the Digital Industry Singapore (DISG) last year to better coordinate Singapore's efforts for the digital industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our suite of value propositions has helped us to grow our tech sector, where we have successfully attracted digital giants, such as Google, Facebook and Alibaba.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: These strong interlinkages among research, innovation and enterprise do not just serve a pure commercial purpose.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, they have been essential to tackling the COVID-19 scourge that we are facing right now, too.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Take Kronikare, an AI startup that is based locally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Kronikare has an AI wound monitoring software to help patients take care of their wounds.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: When COVID-19 struck, Integrated Health System Information (IHiS), the IT arm for our public healthcare sector, partnered Kronikare to quickly re-engineer this core technology to develop an automatic fever detection solution to aid other businesses in the fight against COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Startups like Kronikare play an important role in the innovation ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: They bring new ideas to the table and spur industry to do things differently.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Teo Ser Luck asked about how we identify which startups to invest in.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Investing in startups is inherently risky and the Government does not possess enough information to make these assessments alone.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is why Enterprise Singapore (ESG) co-invests with private sector investors which have the expertise in assessing the commercial value and viability of startups.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For deep-tech startups, it is especially important to have access to such funding that is backed by deep industry knowledge.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Ms Foo Mee Har noted, such startups typically require larger investments and have longer gestation periods because of the multiple iterations of prototyping and pilot production that are needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In fact, for medtech and pharmbio products, they would usually require quite a period of time for clinical trials and validation for safety and efficacy before they can be introduced into the market.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: A portion of the S$300 million will be allocated towards investing in a global Venture Capital (VC) fund, through a new "fund-of-funds" approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This not only increases the availability of investment funds, but also attracts experienced VCs into the Singapore ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our deep-tech startups can then tap on their expertise, knowledge and networks to accelerate their growth, such as seeking guidance on commercialisation and business operations, and importantly, meeting new business partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To encourage funds and fund managers to invest a larger proportion of their funds into Singapore-based startups, we will also extend the relevant tax incentives by five years.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This also includes enhancements, such as expanding the types of investments and incomes incentivised and streamlining of the requirements to invest in Singapore-based enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Chairman, innovation is not only about investing in R&D but also about transforming our industries to be relevant for the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Lee Yi Shyan and Mr Leon Perera have spoken on Industry 4.0 or I4.0.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I4.0 will have a deep impact on our industries, particularly in Manufacturing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Over the years, manufacturing in Singapore has evolved to compete based on the deep skills and capabilities of our companies and our people, and the use of technologies, such as robotics and automation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our initial efforts have allowed us to anchor I4.0 activities from some of the best manufacturers in the world.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This accolade is only offered to advanced manufacturers who show leadership in applying I4.0 technologies to drive change.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We will continue to support companies in their efforts to adopt innovative solutions through a multi-pronged approach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As a start, we launched the Smart Industry Readiness Index (SIRI) and the SIRI Prioritisation Matrix in 2017.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The SIRI Assessments help our companies understand where they are at in their manufacturing transformation journey and to prioritise the improvements they need to make.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Another prong of our strategy is to build platforms that foster interaction and collaboration within the manufacturing ecosystem to adopt I4.0 technologies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Leon Perera and Ms Foo Mee Har asked about networking platforms and industry collaboration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To build a regional community, Singapore has been hosting Industry Transformation Asia Pacific (ITAP), the Asian Edition of Hannover Messe, the world's largest industrial trade fair.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: ITAP has provided a very useful platform to help companies to connect, discover the latest trends in technology and exchange best practices.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We introduced a learning element into the 2019 edition to ensure that our enterprises, workers and even our students were able to learn about I4.0 through guided tours and onsite learning labs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Beyond single touchpoints and events, we are also developing the Jurong Innovation District (JID) as a dedicated advanced manufacturing campus for different players along the value chain, such as researchers, technology providers and businesses, to work together on new ideas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It will also serve as an area for SMEs to collaborate with our multinational corporations and larger enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For our next phase of transformation, we will leverage what we have learnt from our ITMs and explore synergies across the different sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will allow us to identify more opportunities within the clusters to promote innovation, deepen capabilities and, importantly, encourage partnerships.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will be a co-working space to help companies ideate and design their own unique products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: For a start, there will be a focus on equipment design, medtech devices and electromechanical modules.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It will be equipped with the necessary tools for companies to prototype their designs and will have resident design and technology experts to help companies through their innovation journey.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is very useful for SMEs when they do not have the scale or the necessary technical expertise to do this on their own.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, we hope this will be a real boost to our SMEs to raise their innovation capabilities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: After successfully designing their own products, companies can then go on to one of two of the Agency for Science, Technology and Research's (A*STAR's) model factory facilities for pilot production of these new products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To fully seize opportunities in I4.0, companies must also train and upskill their workers; I4.0 is not just about equipment and not just about technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our experience implementing the ITMs has shown that industry transformation is much more effective and pervasive when there is participation and ownership by the workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Labour Movement has been advocating that for I4.0 to succeed, there must be Worker 4.0.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We recently launched the SkillsFuture Work-Learn Bootcamp for Engineer 4.0.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is a three-year pilot programme that will train and place up to 200 engineers in areas, such as lean manufacturing and the Internet of Things.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We have also introduced the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit, with a portion reserved for training and job redesign, to encourage companies to invest in their workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Just as we had turned our vulnerability with water into a strength, we can do likewise with climate change, as Miss Cheryl Chan and Ms Anthea Ong have discussed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Last week, Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean announced the Long-Term Low Emissions Development Strategy (LEDS) which details Singapore's approach towards a low carbon future, and how our industries and Singaporeans can contribute to this global effort.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We have been working closely with companies in the industry to ensure that new or upgraded facilities meet higher levels and higher standards of efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Companies, such as ExxonMobil, are also taking active steps to improve their energy efficiency.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: From 2002 to 2018, ExxonMobil's efforts to reduce their energy consumption in Singapore have led to energy efficiency gains of over 25%.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is equivalent to the removal of more than 550,000 cars from Singapore's roads.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Miss Cheryl Chan would also be pleased to know that there are existing platforms to facilitate exchange of best practices, such as those organised by industry associations like the Sustainable Energy Association of Singapore (SEAS).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We also organise the annual Singapore International Energy Week (SIEW), which brings together global policymakers, think tanks, industry experts and leaders to discuss trends and challenges in the energy landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Given the increasing demand globally for sustainable products and services, there are economic spin-offs to be captured here.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Today, we ensure resilience in our energy supply by encouraging our natural gas importers to diversify and import from multiple sources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This addresses the energy security concerns that Mr Leon Perera has raised.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: On nuclear energy, countries that deploy nuclear energy have to be accountable to their populations and their regions and ensure that high safety and security standards are adhered to.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We are working with ASEAN countries to strengthen cooperation on nuclear safety and emergency preparedness as well as response systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But security is not just about ensuring the robustness of our current energy supply.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is also about looking at our energy future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Hence, we welcome Ms Anthea Ong's suggestions on studying the potential of renewable and alternative energy options.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Such reviews are important because they provide useful insights on how we can work with companies to overcome the growth risks and capture economic opportunities arising from global climate change developments.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: One area of growing interest is the idea of a circular economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: A "circular economy" seeks to improve resource efficiency and recycle resources in a loop to maximise their value.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will allow companies to come together to develop solutions to address these gaps, testbed solutions on Jurong Island and then export these solutions globally.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Individual companies across diverse industries can also benefit from adopting a circular economy concept.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: In the food manufacturing sector, for example, Enterprise Singapore (ESG) has helped to connect food businesses with tech solution providers to convert food waste into higher value products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Last week, I visited SinFooTech, a food technology company co-founded by two young entrepreneurs, Jonathan and Jian Yong.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: When I spoke to Jonathan, he shared how their patented fermentation technology upcycles soy whey, a food waste by-product of tofu manufacturers, into a much higher value-added alcoholic beverage named Sachi.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is the first alcoholic beverage in the world to be made from soy whey and it was fascinating to understand the science behind how soy whey, a waste product from tofu manufacturing, can be converted into an alcoholic drink with a slight fruity, sweet and floral taste.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: And if you have a chance to, you should try it when they finally start their commercial production.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: I am glad to hear that SinFooTech is looking to sell their technology licence overseas and will be setting up a factory to scale up their production of Sachi.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Companies like SinFooTech contribute to Singapore's broader agri-food tech industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This is a sector of growing importance as the world looks for innovative solutions to feed our growing population amidst climate change and resource constraints.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Ms Foo Mee Har asked how the Government will support the development of emerging sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The Government must be prepared to relook at our rules and regulations as we grow new sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As with any new sector, there will be a learning curve for both businesses and the regulator.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: But we must not be afraid to try.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Even before the setting up of AFIP, agencies, such as the Singapore Food Agency (SFA) and ESG, have already been engaging the Singapore Agro-Food Enterprises Federation and other farm operators to address the issues that they have faced with existing regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This includes areas that are important for agri-food tech operations, like building infrastructure, fire safety and other regulatory issues.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: So, we will expand these efforts into a new regulatory sandbox for High Tech farms at AFIP.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: This will allow us to review more regulations for AFIP tenants even more quickly in a more streamlined manner.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: The lessons learnt from the sandbox will then be extended to benefit the wider farming industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As we help our agri-food tech companies to increase their food production capacity through the use of high-tech farming equipment, we must also help them to access new markets and expand their customer base overseas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: As we continue to anchor and seek out new growth areas, new exciting jobs will be created.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: And I hope to see Singaporeans seizing opportunities to work in these exciting sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: To conclude, Mr Chairman, innovation is key to our continued success.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Our resilient and agile economy was not built overnight.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: It is the product of strong and consistent investment over many decades.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: Not every individual project or enterprise will succeed but, collectively, we will move forward.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Dr Koh Poh Koon)
text: We must not be afraid to venture into new frontiers to reap undiscovered rewards, for present and future generations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Chairman, last year, I spoke about the three Ups: Level Up – to strengthen enterprise and workforce capabilities; Scale Up – to help enterprises grow locally and abroad; and Team Up – to enable enterprises to achieve better outcomes together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Our enterprise development schemes provide holistic support to firms of different sizes and at different stages of growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They improve businesses’ and workers’ productivity, and help them to harness technology, innovate, upgrade their skills and internationalise.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Members have highlighted that successful enterprise transformation must go hand-in-hand with skills upgrading and workforce training.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The Deputy Prime Minister mentioned in the Budget Statement that we are introducing the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They can offset out-of-pocket costs for transformation projects.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is over and above the 70% co-funding support under the Enterprise Development Grant and Productivity Solutions Grant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They can also use the credit to help them redesign jobs under the enhanced Productivity Solutions Grant and redeploy workers to more productive and meaningful roles.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Third, firms can use the credit to send their workers for approved training courses, including design-related courses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: I agree with Mr Henry Kwek that our workers can benefit from these skills.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Like technology, design is a critical enabler for innovation and value creation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Design-led approaches can help to solve complex issues and drive business transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Companies like Apple and Dyson have pioneered superior technology.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: But what makes them stand out is their ability to integrate technology with innovative human-centric design.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The DesignSingapore Council (Dsg) is now part of the Economic Development Board and the MTI family.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Dsg launched the Skills Framework for Design last year, together with SSG and Workforce Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will form the Design Education Advisory Committee on 1 April to enhance design skills training for our workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It will be chaired by Mr Low Cheaw Hwei, Head of Design at Philips.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This will complement existing design courses offered by our institutes of higher learning (IHLs) and training providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These add to our existing initiatives to help companies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira asked about the impact of such schemes on productivity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We believe enterprise transformation must start with what the business wants to achieve, what problems it wants to solve and what capabilities it wants to build to reach its goals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The assistance to companies must be enterprise-centric and transformation-focused, based on their needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Our approach has achieved good outcomes so far.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Productivity improvement, innovation and internationalisation remain important pillars of our economy and we must press on with these efforts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In doing so, we will regularly review our policies and schemes and we will continue to engage economists in the private sector and academia.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will help businesses to expand locally and overseas.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Charles Chong asked how SMEs can improve their awareness of the support available and interact easily and efficiently with the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Minister Vivian Balakrishnan spoke about the GoBusiness Licensing portal, a collaboration between the Pro-Enterprise Panel, the Government Technology Agency (GovTech) and the Smart Nation and Digital Government Office (SNDGO).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It provides a simpler, faster and better way for food services companies to apply for all relevant licences.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It is not just about using IT, but as Minister Vivian Balakrishnan explained, to re-engineer our rules and procedures, make them more efficient and more pro-business and save businesses time and money.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We are further developing GoBusiness to be the platform for enterprises to transact with the Government.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For example, applying for change-of-use licence is one challenge faced by many retail businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They may not know which agency to approach and the type of business activities already permitted in their existing premises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Through GoBusiness, a company will be able to check such information by entering its postal code.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The company need not apply for a licence if the activity is already permitted.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: If a licence is required, the company can then proceed to do so through the portal.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The platform will also integrate other transactions beyond licensing, such as helping entrepreneurs to start new businesses and seek Government assistance.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is a joint project by MTI, the Government Technology Agency (GovTech) and the Smart Nation and Digital Government Office (SNDGO), in collaboration with SME Centres and businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Instead of going through multiple sources to gather information on different Government schemes, a company can visit the portal and answer a set of questions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The e-adviser will then recommend suitable schemes based on what the company needs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Those who require further assistance can meet with a Business Advisor at an SME Centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We will enhance our SME Centres as partners for business growth to provide more in-depth support for promising SMEs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Business Advisors will work with these enterprises to develop long-term business plans and chart the next steps together.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Teo Ser Luck asked about the selection criteria for Scale-up SG.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Scale-up SG is for companies of different sizes and industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We have companies from food and beverage, cleaning and retail.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Besides a high level of commitment from the management team to embark on an ambitious growth plan, ESG will look at the company’s track record, its commitment to grow its presence in Singapore, and the potential to create economic spin-offs for Singapore and generate good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The Deputy Prime Minister touched on this as part of Budget 2020.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Douglas Foo asked how the participants will be chosen.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Applicants will be selected based on their demonstration of ambition and commitment and also their growth potential.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: ELT will be designed and delivered together with partners, such as the IHLs, professional firms and banks.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The programme lasts about a year and will include business coaching and practical learning components.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Douglas Foo, who is also President of Singapore Manufacturing Federation, has suggested involving TACs as ELT partners.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Indeed, the business networks of TACs will be very valuable and can support peer learning and collaboration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We look forward to working with our TACs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This brings me to the third prong of our strategy – Team Up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We want companies to Team Up to build deeper capabilities and accelerate their growth.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: One area is the review of Government rules and regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked about our approach in doing so.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Over the years, the Pro-Enterprise Panel (PEP) has partnered industry, businesses and Government agencies to make close to 1,200 improvements in rules and regulations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These have reduced time, effort and costs for businesses, and improved our overall economic competitiveness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: PEP also partners TACs to organise Pro-Enterprise Clinics to identify regulatory pain points and support innovative ideas from businesses.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Earlier, Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon mentioned SinFooTech.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: It is a food technology company which converts soy whey into alcoholic beverages.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The company wanted to set up a research facility to experiment with new products.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: However, it faced high costs, such as distillery licence fees and excise duties.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Customs also extended its pro-rated licence fee framework for microbreweries to distilleries like SinFooTech.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Instead of paying the annual licence fee of $28,000, it can now pay a pro-rated fee of $7,000 per quarter, quarter by quarter.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: If it wants to stop after one or two months because the experiment is not going well, it can get a refund for the remaining licence period.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These features help to lower the entry cost for companies to try new ideas, and also reduce the exit cost if they decide to end their pilot early.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: When we work together with businesses to review our rules and regulations, the improvements will benefit many other enterprises.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: They can launch innovative ideas more quickly and lower their operating costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Government agencies also benefit from having more efficient and business-friendly rules.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We see our role as a gatekeeper and not as a goalkeeper.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: A gatekeeper assesses the risk and decides who to let through and who to turn away, whereas a goalkeeper's mission is to prevent all balls from getting through.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: If we block all new ideas that push against our existing regulatory boundaries or have a risk of failing, there will be no innovation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Listening to feedback and being open to new ideas, feeling comfortable to take calculated risks, and experimenting together with industry partners to turn ideas into reality, these are important aspects of Public Service Transformation, in line with the SG Together Movement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In my maiden speech in Parliament, I spoke about how we should work together to rejuvenate our heartland precincts and shops.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: (In Mandarin):   Over the years, MTI and ESG have teamed up with industry partners to drive heartland precinct rejuvenation and enterprise transformation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Last June, we set up the Heartland Enterprise Centre Singapore (HECS) and set it three main objectives, that is, to uplift precincts, transform enterprises and upskill workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Since then, HECS has done good work and helped many heartland enterprises and Merchants' Associations (MAs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: For example, it helped the Ang Mo Kio MA to promote and broadcast its Chinese New Year festivities on social media, increasing footfall to the precinct; the Bedok MA to add vibrancy to the town centre through lighting installations and displays; and the Chong Pang MA to develop a dedicated online marketplace for shops in the precinct to increase their sales.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Under this programme, MAs can receive dedicated support from ESG, HDB, and HECS to develop and implement 4-year action plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: These plans will cover upgrading of common area infrastructure, organising placemaking activities, and the upgrading of enterprises and workers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, the Government will help businesses and workers tide over the immediate challenges due to COVID-19.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: We are also committed to supporting businesses at different stages of growth to transform and prepare for the future, so that our companies and our workers will emerge stronger.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Through economic growth, we have achieved employment growth and wage growth for our workers, and improved the lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: Real wages have grown by 3% per year in the last 10 years and young people are able to secure good jobs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: In the 2019 graduate employment survey results for university and polytechnic students, more than 90% found employment within six months of graduation, with higher median salaries than previous batches.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: The outcomes we have achieved are the result of effective policies, hard work and good governance, underpinned by a stable political system and strong tripartite partnerships, as well as a forward-looking Government that plans long term and does not shy away from telling the truth, even if it is unpopular, a Government which places Singaporeans at the heart of everything we do.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is an important component of our Singapore Story: how we grow as a nation, how every generation builds on the foundations laid by previous generations and takes the country further to benefit future generations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: This is how we must continue to forge ahead – always striving for improvement – Keeping Singapore domestically united and globally connected; and never giving up in the face of adversity.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Trade and Industry (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
text: As we say in Hokkien, "pah buay si", and if I may add, "pah si pun boh zao" or to have a never-say-die attitude in Hokkien.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Trade and Industry (Dr Tan Wu Meng)
text: Mr Chairman, Sir, if I may beg your indulgence, in case we overrun by a little bit.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We appreciate the good work of our TACs.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: They are a store of social capital with their institutional memory, shared experience and industry networks.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: I agree with Mr Douglas Foo that our TACs help the Government to better understand the needs of our business community, and partner us to develop industry.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Mr Douglas Foo, Mr Teo Ser Luck and Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about the Government's plans to help TACs and companies expand into new markets.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: To start, SBF will organise seminars, trade fairs and business missions to help businesses grow in Southeast Asia and they will do this for emerging markets as well across the Middle East, Central Asia and Africa.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: SBF's international advisory centre will also answer companies' enquiries about internationalisation and the use of FTAs.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Because when our businesses take flight, it grows our economy's international wing of the economy.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: It creates more opportunities for fellow Singaporeans at home and abroad and, furthermore, COVID-19 has also been a stark reminder of the need to diversify across multiple markets.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The Government will equip TACs with more resources to support companies in their transformation journey.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: This is to help TACs engage experienced executives to guide companies in business transformation and growth.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Participating TACs will help to identify, engage and match the executives with companies based on their needs.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Our TACs will also need to upgrade their workforce and capabilities, which Mr Douglas Foo asked about.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: TACs can tap on the LEAD programme to strengthen their leadership and secretariats, and improve organisational processes.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Several have done so, such as the Federation of Merchants' Associations Singapore and the Singapore Indian Chamber of Commerce and Industry and there will be many more to come.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We asked the two retailers to show us the basis of their prices.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The retailers subsequently apologised and reduced their prices.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan also suggested ways for the Government to deter unfair practices.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We will study his suggestions, but there is also a need to balance between consumers' interests and a pro-business environment, because our fellow Singaporeans include entrepreneurs and business owners as well.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: First, review our laws on competition and consumer protection to ensure they continue to be effective in deterring unfair practices.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: This will help consumers make better decisions and help companies to continue competing on a level playing field.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCCS) has developed a set of guidelines on the Dos and Don'ts in price transparency for all consumer-facing industries.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: This will reduce the risk of consumers being misled.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: These guidelines will apply to both online and offline transactions and will be published in due course.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Mr Lim Biow Chuan had raised the question of charge-back issues.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: I assure Mr Lim Biow Chuan that consumers can seek assistance on charge-back issues through their credit card issuers' hotline.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And there are also ongoing efforts to raise awareness on the charge-back process.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The websites of credit card issuers, the Association of Banks in Singapore, the Consumers Association of Singapore (CASE) and MoneySENSE – all these have Frequently Asked Questions on the process of resolving common credit card disputes, including charge-backs.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: CASE piloted the Price Kaki app featuring crowdsourcing insights on prices at supermarkets and hawker centres across Tampines, Toa Payoh and Jurong West starting from September 2019.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: It means that people at supermarkets, people looking for cooked food, can share information about prices and bargains, so that other users can share the information from it as well.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Since its launch, we have seen 15,000 registered users, more than half a million crowdsourced entries from users.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And all this, across just three towns in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Imagine if we had it across the island.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: I am pleased to announce that the Price Kaki app will be rolled out across Singapore in the coming months.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: With this crowdsourcing network, everyone can have a buddy, everyone can be a buddy.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: You might say, "Long zhong wu kaki, long zhong si kaki" or we all have buddies in Hokkien.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Furthermore, Price Kaki helps people who have less time, who are less aware of market prices, who are less experienced shoppers.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: It is an app for everyone across all walks of life, but especially people who may be starting with less.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: It is a progressive move to build a fairer, more equitable society.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We hope you can benefit from the app, whether contributing as a kaki or benefiting as a price kaki.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: (In Mandarin):   We understand and care for your concerns with regard to cost of living issues.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: CASE will be launching the Consumer Empowerment Panel (CEP) in April to look into matters on cost of living.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: The panel will work together with associations, unions and grassroots leaders, to engage and help consumers like you stretch your hard-earned dollar.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And sometimes, the world outside throws challenges at us.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And to face these challenges, it takes all of us, because when we pull together, we are stronger.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: In Mandarin, "众人同心，其利断金"。In Malay, "berat sama dipikul, ringan sama dijinjing".

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: We have seen this in the fight against COVID-19.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Nurses and doctors on the frontlines, working day and night, round the clock, to protect us from the outbreak.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Volunteers, at mask distribution centres in the community, delivering masks to the homes of neighbours who are less mobile.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Our TACs and companies are doing their part, too.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Mr Chairman, in conclusion, we are all in this together – you and me, the people around us, our TACs, our fellow Singaporean businesses, the Government.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And this is how, as a nation, we can survive and thrive, no matter what odds the world throws at us.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: This is how we keep on creating new possibilities for a better, brighter Singapore.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: This is how, together, we can make a difference, because together, we can, and together, we will overcome.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Yesterday, the Restaurant Association Singapore issued a statement reminding landlords to pass on the property tax rebates that they will be enjoying to the retailers.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: There are other retailers who are not happy that the landlords are not making it clear on passing on these rebates.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: So, can I ask the Minister if he is concerned that the good intention of the Government, which is to help the retailers impacted by the COVID-19 outbreak, is not being followed through by the landlords?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: And whether any measures can be taken to urge the landlords to pass on the rebates?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: While stifling regulations can work against the enterprise ecosystem and add costs, but we also know that adequate regulations do protect consumers, set high standards, build trust.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: In our context, regulations can be both a competitive advantage and a competitive disadvantage.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State to share a bit more where we should lean towards and where is that sweet spot?

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Mr Chairman, let me take the first question and Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat will answer the second one.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: We are all in this together – the whole Singapore economy depends on businesses – the landlords, the retailers, everyone working together.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: On the positive side, we have seen landlords who have proactively gone out of their way to share the rebates with their tenants.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, a few of them have gone out of their way to take into account the tenants' reduced turnover to help them more, and I applaud these landlords.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: But on the other hand, it has also come to our attention that there are some landlords who are still taking a bit of time to roll out their packages.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And I would say this to the landlord.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: The relationship between the landlord and the tenant is a long-term relationship.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: When the tenants do well, the landlords do well; when the landlords do well, they need to share it with the tenants.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: This is a long-term relationship and Singapore is not that big an economy.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: Every one of us will have long memories of who are those who have come forward to do their part for their business partner in this difficult moment and who are those that have taken a very short-term perspective to this.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: ESG will continue to work closely to arbitrate between the landlords and also the tenants.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: In fact, I must thank ESG officers who have been working very hard over the last one week, day and night, trying to urge both sides to come to terms with each other.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: At the same time, I must say that, for the tenants who are affected, they are not all affected equally and we should try to give a bit more help to those that are more affected by the downturn caused by COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
text: And if we can do this all together, we will go past this stronger together.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Mr Liang Eng Hwa for his supplementary question.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Indeed, there is a need to strike a balance and that is why I use the analogy of a gatekeeper.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Someone needs to watch the risks, on what are the downsides.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And every proposal that comes needs to be assessed carefully.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: What is the impact on stakeholders, consumers and other businesses?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, this is a process which we do on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Whenever we get a proposal from businesses, we will work together with the regulatory agencies to understand what is the rationale for the current rules, can it be improved and enhanced, can the process be better?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The example I would give Mr Liang Eng Hwa is this: you build a ship and the safest place for the ship may be to park it in the harbour.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But we know that is not why we built ships.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We built ships because we want the ship to be able to bring us to different places around the world, but the ships need to be safe.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, how do you do it in such a way that will allow us to look for new opportunities and new areas but still remain safe, the quality must still be maintained?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Because that is a very important part of our economic competitiveness.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Our trusted brand name, quality assurance, people think that when they walk into Singapore, they have the confidence that things work well here.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: And what we want to avoid are the two extremes – free for all; nothing at all.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: There is a sweet spot, as Mr Liang Eng Hwa mentioned, somewhere in the middle.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But where that sweet spot is, that one, we have to evaluate on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is why it is so important for us to do this in partnership because when we understand what the pain points are, based on the feedback from our businesses, and we understand also the rationale for the rules and regulations from our regulatory agencies, then there is scope for us to see how we can innovate together and improve the rules and processes together.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, that is where we are aiming for.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa asked me about where is the balance we want to strike.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: I think that balance is what we want to aim for and the process will be as part of Public Service transformation, as part of engaging our businesses, our TACs, to do it together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, I thank Senior Minister of State Chee Hong Tat for the reply to the cut.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: First, I would like to understand the Ministry's findings on the effect of grant schemes a bit better.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: In other words, what is the marginal contribution of public funding?

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: Because the concern here is that it could just be a substitute for private funding.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: In that case, not a good use of taxpayer money.

speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
text: This was in the cut but not directly addressed just now.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: A large part of it – actually, the main part of it – is due to the hard work and the entrepreneurial drive of our businesses.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: The business owners must be, first, at the forefront of this.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: If they do not have good ideas, they do not know how to transform their businesses, they do not know what to do with the various resources that they have, I do not think any amount of Government grants will help them.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, that is why we pay a lot of attention to helping businesses with good growth potential, with the commitment and ambition, to see how we can help them to go further.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But it has to start with the business owner having that drive, the ideas, the resilience and the resourcefulness to be able to pool these ideas together and produce a service or a product that will meet the needs of its customers.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, because it is a residual indicator, the changes in TFP, first, it could be due to a range of different reasons; and second, it is more meaningful to look at it over a longer period of time because of the ups and downs.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: Because of that, we do not just look at TFP; we also look at other indicators to guide us, in terms of whether our schemes are working, to provide the feedback on whether our schemes are working.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: These are indicators, such as value added, jobs created – especially jobs for Singaporeans – investments that we could attract and also what is the value added per worker.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We use a mixture of indicators to provide a more complete picture.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to thank Senior Minister of State Koh Poh Koon for addressing my cut, particularly in terms of the economic transition to decarbonisation.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: Do we know when the risk to the economy from high carbon sectors will become pertinent?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: What are our plans to invest in deep industrial efficiency, carbon capture utilisation and storage (CCUS), or low carbon hydrogen to not only just mitigate the risk to our economy, but also to create new jobs?

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I assume a large number of them are actually locals.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
text: I am wondering how are we reskilling these high carbon industry jobs to prepare for the kind of jobs that we can expect which we do not know now, in the next decade, as Minister Chan Chun Sing mentioned.

speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: The risks – when will the risks to our economy from this high carbon sector become pertinent?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: At this moment, the situation is still evolving because the technology for many of the low carbon alternatives are still quite nascent.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: They are still not exactly mainstream, things like CCUS, hydrogen fuel cell technology, for example.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: All these things are still technologically undergoing development and they have not gone to mainstream yet.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, I do not think we have reached the inflection point where we need to actually transit aggressively into alternative energy sources.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For new jobs, one of the key things is to make sure that we continue to work on our ITM together with the industry.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The ITM for the energy and chemical sector is a tripartite effort between the oil majors or the people owning the refineries in the energy sector, together with the union as well as the workers.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The idea is to make sure that we involve these tripartite partners into looking at what their transition plans would be over the longer term, and then working out step-by-step what kinds of new jobs would be created in the interim, what kinds of skills are needed and then very, very targetedly training the workers today to continue to take on new skillsets so that, as the new jobs come about, whether it is through efficiency measures, putting in new technology that changes the way they work, then the skills of the workers are relevant for these new jobs that come about.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, I hope that gives Members the kind of sense of where we are implementing some of these technological changes to our workforce.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I hope that answers the bulk of the Member's questions.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Liang Eng Hwa, would you like to withdraw your amendment?

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: Indeed, our economy is facing among the most daunting challenges and circumstances in recent years with serious implications on jobs and business survivability.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: So, it is reassuring that MTI as well as the Budget 2020 measures are there to help the businesses to tide over this period.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: We wish the MTI team every success in steering our economy forward and to emerge stronger.

speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
text: With that, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment, Sir.
